scheme_name: Community Canning & Training On Fruit Preservation
description:
The Community Canning & Training on Fruit Preservation scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2018. 

The initiative is part of the larger effort to enhance the income of farmers and promote the preservation of fruits. 

The scheme aims to provide training to rural women and farmers in fruit preservation techniques. 

The primary objective is to reduce post-harvest losses of fruits which can be as high as 30 to 40 percent in some regions. 

By providing training, the government aims to empower women and create self-employment opportunities. 

The scheme also seeks to promote the use of local fruits and enhance their value through preservation techniques. 

The target beneficiaries include rural women, self-help groups, and farmers. 

The scheme specifically focuses on women as they play a crucial role in managing household nutrition and income. 

The training sessions are designed to cover various aspects of fruit preservation including canning, bottling, and jam-making. 

The government aims to conduct training programs in at least 500 blocks across the country within the first two years of the scheme. 

The expected outcome is to train approximately 50,000 women in the first phase. 

Each training program typically lasts for about 5 days. 

Participants receive hands-on training and learn about the scientific methods of fruit preservation. 

The training also includes information on hygiene, food safety, and marketing of preserved products. 

Upon completion of the training, participants are encouraged to start their own canning units. 

The government provides financial assistance to set up these units. 

The assistance can be up to INR 1 lakh for setting up a community canning unit. 

The scheme also promotes the establishment of community canning centers. 

These centers serve as hubs for training and production. 

They are equipped with the necessary tools and equipment for fruit preservation. 

The government collaborates with various agricultural universities and research institutions for technical support. 

The eligibility criteria for beneficiaries include being a resident of a rural area. 

Participants must be part of a self-help group or willing to form one. 

There are no specific age limits but preference is given to women between the ages of 18 to 45 years. 

Income criteria are not strictly defined but beneficiaries are generally from low-income households. 

The application process involves submitting a form to the local agricultural department. 

Required documents include proof of residence, identity proof, and details of the self-help group. 

The application can be submitted online through the official government portal or in person at local offices. 

Once the application is approved, beneficiaries are notified about the training schedule. 

Training sessions are conducted by trained facilitators from agricultural departments or NGOs. 

The government aims to conduct these training programs at least twice a year in each block. 

The disbursement of financial assistance occurs after the successful completion of the training. 

Beneficiaries must submit a project report detailing their proposed canning unit. 

The report is evaluated by the local agricultural department before funds are released. 

The scheme has seen participation from various states including Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu. 

In Maharashtra alone, over 10,000 women have been trained since the launch of the scheme. 

The impact of the scheme is measured through the increase in income of the beneficiaries. 

Reports indicate that trained women have seen an increase in their household income by up to 30 percent. 

The government also tracks the number of canning units established under the scheme. 

As of 2023, over 1,000 community canning units have been set up across the country. 

These units not only provide employment but also contribute to local economies. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from participants who report improved skills and confidence. 

Women trained under the scheme have started selling their products in local markets. 

The government provides marketing support through exhibitions and fairs. 

They also facilitate connections with local retailers and wholesalers. 

The scheme aligns with the National Policy for Women Empowerment which emphasizes economic independence. 

It also supports the goals of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture. 

The implementation of the scheme is overseen by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The department of horticulture in each state plays a crucial role in executing the program. 

Contact details for inquiries can be found on the official Ministry of Agriculture website. 

The scheme is part of a broader strategy to enhance food security and nutrition in rural areas. 

It addresses both the economic and social empowerment of women. 

The government continues to monitor and evaluate the scheme to ensure its effectiveness. 

Future plans include expanding the scheme to include more fruits and preservation techniques. 

The scheme is expected to evolve based on feedback from participants and changing market demands. 

Overall, the Community Canning & Training on Fruit Preservation scheme represents a significant step towards empowering rural women and reducing food wastage. 

It combines skill development with economic opportunities, making it a vital initiative in India's rural development landscape. 

Through this scheme, the government aims to create a sustainable model for fruit preservation that benefits both producers and consumers. 

The focus on community involvement ensures that the benefits are widespread and inclusive. 

The scheme not only addresses immediate economic needs but also fosters long-term sustainability in agriculture. 

By enhancing the skills of rural women, the government is investing in the future of rural communities. 

The Community Canning & Training on Fruit Preservation scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to improving livelihoods and promoting gender equality in India.
